topic: Mutual Fund and ETF Fees and Expenses
subtopic: ETF Premiums and Discounts to Net Asset Value
source_evidence: An ETF share is trading at a premium when its market price is higher than the NAV per share. An ETF share is trading at a discount when its market price is lower than the NAV per share.
question: What does it mean for an ETF to trade at a premium or discount to its net asset value (NAV) per share?
answer: An ETF trades at a premium when its market price is higher than its NAV per share, and at a discount when its market price is lower. As a result, when buying or selling, an investor may pay or receive more or less than the NAV per share.
